en.html:
...Night grew late.

Dinner finished, Kanae opened the enormous case she had carried since our first meeting. I had wondered what on earth it contained. Lid up, mystery solved. Double bass.

Double-bass case ke andar double bass. An astonishingly honest arrangement. My suspicion had spent its time achieving nothing.

Why an occupation officer travelled with such an instrument, that question remained. Perhaps surprise was unnecessary. Personal attendant also she had brought.

Ordinary conventions appeared to be making suggestions to her. She was free to hear them or continue on her way.

en.html:
A formidable enemy outside.
A considerable wound upon myself.

Phir bhi, warmth. A little peace.
...And suddenly I nearly remembered what I must not remember.

Woh door ka manzar—no. That distant scene, not to be recalled.
This reality, the fight before me, not to be forgotten.

Aaram karo, abhi. Rest for now.
But no settling into this peace.
Tomorrow's battle. For that only.

For now—
sleep.

en.html:
Slightly dreamy, Fuki returned to the washing. Beside her I continued splitting wood.

Several days supplied already. Thoda aur, a little reserve would not hurt.

Yagenta worked inside. Some part of the house or another required repairing; morning routine, apparently. Ootori and her attendant had returned to the village last night.

'We must think of some way, mustn't we.'

Kanae's parting words. Haan. Left alone, the magistrate and his men would buy time and work upon GHQ.

Allow it, and the village would not be saved. My objective also would probably fail. Leisurely, leisurely, until the time arrived and our leisure had killed the whole undertaking.

Koi tareeqa. Some way to pull the enemy out of that forest.

The thought and the firewood, I worked on both. Wood at least had the courtesy to split when struck.

en.html:
Her silence reached me. An odd thing to receive, silence, but that was what arrived. Not a broken connection. Someone deliberately saying nothing. I could feel it somewhere in the brain joined to the tsurugi.

An ordinary person could keep quiet at some distance. Muramasa could keep quiet directly inside my head. The absence of words was becoming very difficult not to listen to.

せよ、全て俺一人の物だ。お前には何もない・・・・・・・・。
　当然だろう。奴隷に責任を押し付ける主人

en.html:
The hard voice stopped ringing in my head. I returned my attention to what my eyes were seeing. Quite a pile of firewood had come into existence while I was occupied elsewhere.

Three people in this house. With this much, fuel should not trouble them for some time. The discussion had produced no warmth, but apparently the accompanying work would.

Holding the next log, Funa looked up at me with a question in her eyes. I nodded.

脳内に打ち響く硬質の声が絶える。
　意識を視界へ戻す――ふと見れば、積み上げられた
薪は随分な量に達していた。

　わずか三人の暮らし、これだけあれば当分炊きつけ
に困ることはないだろう。
　次の薪を抱えて問うように見上げてくる幼い視線へ、
頷きを返す。

en.html:
Yagenta"Mido. ...Arre, quite a quantity you have made."
Kageaki"The young lady assisted me. The work went quickly."
Funa"I helped!"
Yagenta"Haan, shabaash. ...Now, Mido. Can I leave the house in your care for a little while?"
Kageaki"Going somewhere?"
Yagenta"Down to the foot of the mountain. I should be back by noon."
Kageaki"Understood. The house is in my care."
Yagenta"Troubling you again. I leave it to you."

景明「御令嬢にお手伝い頂いたので。 　手早く片付いてしまいました」
ふな「てつだったー！」
弥源太「そうか。よくやったな。 　……それで御堂。少し留守を頼んでも良い かな」
景明「どちらかへお出掛けですか」
弥源太「うむ。ちと麓まで下りてくる。 　昼までには戻れるだろう」
景明「承知致しました。 　留守をお預かりします」
弥源太「すまんな。 　よろしく頼む」

en.html:
Steadily the old man went down the mountain path. A small cloth-wrapped bundle tucked under one arm.

Something white protruded from it.
White—a flower.

A visit to a grave, perhaps? A little late for the equinox observances...

　白い――花。

　<ruby>彼岸会<rt>ひがんえ</rt></ruby>にはいささか遅過ぎるが……。
